overview: Robinhood operates a vertically integrated, mobile-first financial services platform offering commission-free trading in equities, options, cryptocurrency, futures, and event contracts (prediction markets), alongside a subscription service (Robinhood Gold), banking, credit card, and wealth management (Robinhood Strategies, TradePMR) products. Founded in 2013 to 'democratize finance for all,' the company serves primarily retail investors in the U.S., with expanding operations in the U.K., EU, and following acquisitions, Canada (WonderFi) and institutional crypto markets (Bitstamp). Revenue roughly tripled from $1.87B (FY2023) to $4.47B (FY2025) as the company swung from a net loss to GAAP profitability, driven by transaction-based revenue (options, crypto, equities, and rapidly scaling event contracts), net interest income on margin/cash balances, and subscription/other revenue.

business_model.summary: Robinhood earns the majority of revenue from transaction-based fees (payment for order flow / rebates on options, equities, and crypto order routing, plus commissions on futures and event contracts), supplemented by net interest revenue on margin loans, cash sweep, and segregated cash, and a smaller but growing subscription/other segment (Robinhood Gold, Gold Card, proxy fees, Trump Accounts services). As of Q3 2026 (nine months), transaction-based revenue was 60% of total net revenue, net interest revenue 31%, and other revenue 10%. Within transaction-based revenue, options remain the largest single line (~26% of total net revenue over 9M-2026) but event contracts have grown explosively (1% to 12% of total net revenue in one year) while crypto transaction revenue has fallen sharply (~21% to ~9%) amid lower retail crypto trading activity and rebate rates.

revenue_streams.name: Net interest revenue (margin, cash sweep, credit card, corporate cash)

business_model.customer_type: B2C retail investors (primary), with expanding B2B/institutional exposure via Bitstamp (institutional crypto exchange) and TradePMR (RIA custody platform)
business_model.geographic_mix: Primarily U.S.; expanding U.K. brokerage (RHUK), EU crypto (RHEU, enlarged by Bitstamp), Canada (WonderFi/Bitbuy/Coinsquare), and planned Indonesia and Singapore (APAC HQ) operations. Non-U.S. funded customers surpassed 1 million following WonderFi close (June 2026).

competitive_position.market_position: Leading U.S. retail brokerage app by customer count and engagement among younger/first-time investors; a newer but fast-growing entrant in prediction markets (event contracts) and a top-tier U.S. retail crypto trading venue, though losing share in both crypto trading activity and prediction-market volume (Robinhood's share of Kalshi-routed volume reportedly fell from near 60% to under 25% within six months in early 2026) to competitors building out their own exchanges.

moat_factors.description: Self-clearing broker-dealer, proprietary order routing, own money-transmitter and FCM licenses, and (via Rothera/Rothera E&C) a majority-owned CFTC-licensed exchange/clearinghouse for event contracts — reduces reliance on third parties and supports unit economics
Robinhood is synonymous with retail investing in the U.S.; strong word-of-mouth growth and cultural relevance among younger investors
First-mover on commission-free trading, 24-hour markets, fractional shares, and (recently) short selling and index options; fast iteration cycle supported by cloud-native stack
Gold subscription bundles trading, banking, credit card, margin, and advisory benefits, increasing wallet share and switching costs as customers age into higher balances
Broad suite of licenses (broker-dealer, FCM, money transmitter, investment adviser, EU MiCA/MiFID via Bitstamp/RHEU) raises barriers to new entrants but also creates compliance burden

weaknesses: Still significant reliance on transaction-based revenue tied to volatile retail trading/crypto volumes
Does not wholly own or control Rothera (event-contracts JV with SIG), limiting strategic control of a key growth driver
Crypto trading revenue has declined sharply (down ~48% YoY for 9M-2026) as retail crypto enthusiasm cooled and larger players (Coinbase, Kalshi) compete
Prediction markets exposed to an unsettled, multi-state legal/regulatory patchwork that could restrict or ban key products (sports event contracts) in various states
Smaller scale than legacy brokerages (Schwab, Fidelity) in total assets and advisory depth despite customer-count leadership

growth_drivers: Prediction markets / event contracts: revenue grew from ~1% to ~12% of total net revenue within a year; management calls it the fastest-growing business in company history, with Rothera E&C (acquired MIAXdx, Jan 2026) building proprietary exchange/clearing capacity and a new Crypto.com routing agreement (Sept 2026) for up to 10% equity stake

Robinhood Gold subscriber growth (+34% YoY to 5.18M in Q3-2026) driving subscription revenue, margin lending, and cross-sell into Robinhood Banking (invite-only, via Coastal Bank) and the Gold Card (600K+ cardholders)

Wealth management/advisory expansion via TradePMR (RIA custody, closed Feb 2025) and Robinhood Strategies, targeting 'multigenerational advisory' as the next-gen customer base ages and accumulates assets

International expansion: U.K. brokerage (stocks and shares ISAs), EU crypto/stock tokens, Bitstamp-driven European and institutional crypto expansion, and new entries into Canada (WonderFi/Bitbuy/Coinsquare, closed June 2026) and planned Indonesia (PT Buana Capital Sekuritas, PT Pedagang Aset Kripto) and Singapore (APAC HQ)
AI integration (Robinhood Cortex, AI-native advisory products) and continued buildout of Robinhood Legend for active traders
Net interest income tailwind from larger margin book and credit card balances, partially offsetting lower cash-sweep yields in a falling-rate environment
S&P 500 index inclusion (effective September 22, 2025) increased passive-fund ownership and market visibility

business.risk: Revenue cyclicality tied to trading/crypto volumes
business.description: Transaction-based revenue (60% of total) is highly dependent on market volatility, 'meme' trading episodes, and retail sentiment; crypto transaction revenue fell ~48% YoY in 9M-2026 as activity cooled

business.risk: Customer and revenue concentration risk in options/event contracts
business.description: Options (~26%) and now event contracts (~12%) are large, concentrated revenue drivers; a slowdown in active-trader engagement or contract availability would materially affect revenue

business.risk: Competitive share loss in prediction markets and crypto
business.description: Robinhood's share of routed volume on Kalshi fell sharply in early 2026 as competitors (Kalshi's own app, Coinbase, Crypto.com) scale their own venues
Robinhood does not wholly own or operationally control Rothera/Rothera E&C (JV with Susquehanna/SIG), a key growth vehicle for event contracts

financial.risk: Net interest revenue sensitive to rate cuts
financial.description: Net interest revenue (31% of total) declined in Q3-2026 as cash-sweep and segregated-cash yields fell; management explicitly flags anticipated Fed rate cuts as a headwind despite a September 2026 rate increase

financial.risk: Rising credit provisions from credit card growth
financial.description: Provision for credit losses roughly tripled YoY (Q3-2026) on growth of the Gold Card and Credit Card Funding Trust receivables
$2.7B long-term borrowings outstanding including 2029 convertible notes; manageable given $5.8B cash and strong net capital surplus at broker-dealer subsidiaries

regulatory.description: Reliance on payment for order flow and rebate-based routing remains subject to SEC/FINRA best-execution rules and potential future bans or restructuring of PFOF-like practices

Extensive, unresolved multi-state litigation and enforcement actions (Massachusetts, Wisconsin, Kentucky, Nevada, New Jersey, Michigan, Ohio, Washington, tribal gaming claims) alleging sports-related event contracts constitute illegal gambling; outcomes of CFTC preemption arguments and pending circuit court/Supreme Court review could force product withdrawal in multiple states and have already forced Robinhood to cease new sports contracts in Nevada, Michigan, and Ohio
Uncertain status of specific cryptocurrencies as 'securities' and staking-services characterization could trigger SEC/state enforcement

regulatory.risk: State and federal tax treatment of event contracts
regulatory.description: Unclear federal excise tax treatment of event contracts and new state-specific prediction-market taxes (Illinois, North Carolina, Kentucky) create potential retroactive liability

NY AG brokerage execution-quality probe, FINRA/FDIC examinations (BOATS outage), cash-sweep interest class actions (settled in principle), Early 2021 trading-restriction matters, IPO disclosure litigation pending cert petition at SCOTUS
Robinhood Banking depends on partner bank Coastal Bank; increased federal regulatory focus on bank-as-a-service arrangements could constrain growth or partnership continuity

macro.risk: Retail trading sentiment and market volatility
macro.description: A broad market downturn or extended period of low retail engagement would reduce trading-driven revenue across equities, options, and crypto
Falling rates compress net interest margin on cash sweep and segregated cash balances, a meaningful share of revenue
Revenue directly tied to crypto price volatility and notional trading volume, which have both declined materially from 2025 peaks

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Online brokerage and retail trading industry is mature in equities/options but still rapidly evolving in crypto and the newly-emergent prediction/event-contracts category, which multiple analysts (e.g., Bernstein) project to grow substantially; regulatory outcomes (state gambling-law preemption by CFTC) are a major unresolved swing factor for the latter.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — revenue is closely tied to retail trading volumes, market volatility ('meme' episodes), and crypto price cycles, making results volatile quarter to quarter
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high; roughly a third of revenue is net interest income on margin loans, cash sweep, and credit card balances, which is pressured by Fed rate cuts
key_input_costs: Payment/rebate economics from market-maker order routing

recent_developments.event: Total net revenue rose 12% YoY to $1.424B; net income attributable to Robinhood fell 16% YoY to $468M ($0.51 diluted EPS) despite revenue growth, as operating expenses rose 16% and other income swung to a $60M loss from RVI/RVII mark-to-market

Event contracts (prediction markets) revenue surged 541% YoY to $173M in the quarter; CEO Tenev said Robinhood Prediction Markets crossed 4 billion event contracts traded all-time, with over 2 billion traded in Q3 alone, calling it the fastest-growing business in company history
Cryptocurrency transaction revenue fell 55% YoY to $120M as crypto trading activity and notional volume per trader declined; Total Platform Assets' crypto component fell from $51.1B to $37.9B YoY

Entered agreements with Crypto.com under which Robinhood may receive up to a 10% equity interest over three years in exchange for routing event contracts to Crypto.com's CFTC-regulated exchange (CDNA/OG.com)
Closed ~$180M acquisition of WonderFi (Bitbuy, Coinsquare), entering the Canadian crypto market and pushing non-U.S. funded customers past 1 million
Sold down ownership in Robinhood Ventures Fund I (RVI) from ~52% to ~49%, triggering deconsolidation and a $106M gain
Rothera (JV with Susquehanna/SIG) acquired 90% of MIAXdx, renamed Rothera E&C, to build an independent CFTC-licensed exchange/clearinghouse for event contracts
CFO Jason Warnick announced retirement (Oct 30, 2025); Shiv Verma (SVP Finance/Treasurer) named successor CFO, with Warnick transitioning to a strategic advisor role through September 2026
Robinhood added to the S&P 500 index (alongside AppLovin, Emcor), driving a one-day ~6-13% share price pop on passive-fund buying

Closed acquisition of Bitstamp, a globally-scaled crypto exchange serving retail and institutional clients, accelerating European expansion and adding institutional products (on-exchange lending, off-exchange settlement, perpetual futures)
Closed acquisition of TradePMR, an RIA custody and portfolio management platform, expanding Robinhood's wealth-management/advisory footprint

Extensive multi-state litigation and enforcement activity over sports-related event contracts; Robinhood/RHD agreed to cease new sports event contracts in Nevada (Dec 2025), Michigan, and Ohio (Nov 2026) pending appeals, while continuing to litigate CFTC-preemption theory in other states (Connecticut, New Jersey, Wisconsin, Kentucky, Massachusetts, Washington)

Stock has been volatile and well off its 2026 highs; shares traded around $84 in early November 2026 versus a 52-week high near $150 and low near $64, with analyst price targets spread widely (roughly $57 to $166) reflecting disagreement over crypto/prediction-market trajectory

items.notes: Narrowed from prior $2.675B-$2.775B range given in Q2-2026 guidance; tightened toward the lower end

items.target: Headwind expected from anticipated Fed rate cuts
items.notes: Management explicitly flagged that anticipated future Fed rate cuts would negatively impact net interest revenues and customer cash-balance returns, despite a September 2026 Fed Funds Rate increase

items.target: Continued rapid expansion; no specific numeric target disclosed in filings
items.notes: Management (CEO Tenev) characterizes event contracts as the fastest-growing business in company history and a top strategic priority, backed by Rothera E&C exchange build-out; some analysts (e.g., Bernstein) model triple-digit percentage revenue growth from this line, though this is an external estimate, not formal guidance

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Vlad Tenev emphasized prediction markets' rapid growth (4 billion-plus event contracts traded all-time, 2 billion in Q3 alone) and ongoing build-out of Robinhood Banking, wealth/advisory (TradePMR), and a 'super app' strategy spanning trading, banking, and investing. On crypto softness, Tenev said the company is 'not getting distracted by short-term [price] fluctuations,' framing the business as a long-term platform play rather than a trade on crypto cycles. Management continues to caution that rate cuts will pressure net interest revenue and that results will remain volatile quarter to quarter given dependence on trading activity and Net Deposits growth (which slowed to 17% annualized in Q3-2026 from 29% a year earlier).

bull_case: Explosive, high-margin growth in prediction markets/event contracts (541% YoY revenue growth in Q3-2026) represents a new, large addressable market with Robinhood positioned as an early leader via Rothera E&C's own exchange/clearinghouse infrastructure

Successful transition to sustained GAAP profitability (FY2025 net income $1.88B) with a growing, diversified revenue base (Gold subscriptions, banking, wealth management, credit card) reducing pure dependence on trading commissions

Large and growing funded customer base (28.7M) and Total Platform Assets ($395.9B, +19% YoY) provide a long runway for cross-selling higher-margin services (Gold, Strategies, Banking) as the 'next generation' of investors ages into more assets

International and institutional expansion (Bitstamp, TradePMR, WonderFi, planned Indonesia/Singapore entries) diversifies revenue geographically and extends reach into underpenetrated advisory and crypto segments
S&P 500 index inclusion and improved capital markets credibility have broadened the investor base and increased passive ownership, supporting a higher valuation floor
bear_case: Core crypto trading revenue has collapsed (down ~48% YoY for 9M-2026), raising questions about the durability of retail engagement and Robinhood's competitive position versus Coinbase and other crypto-native platforms

Prediction markets face a serious, unresolved multi-state legal and regulatory threat — numerous lawsuits and enforcement actions allege sports-related event contracts are illegal gambling, and Robinhood has already been forced to cease offering new sports contracts in several states pending appeals that could go either way at the Ninth/Sixth Circuits or the Supreme Court
Revenue remains highly cyclical and sentiment-driven; Net Deposits growth has decelerated sharply (17% annualized in Q3-2026 vs. 29% a year prior), suggesting the pace of asset-gathering is slowing
Falling interest rates are a direct headwind to net interest revenue (31% of total revenue), a line that already declined YoY in Q3-2026 despite balance growth

Robinhood does not fully control its fastest-growing business (Rothera is a joint venture with SIG) and faces intensifying competition for prediction-market volume share, which has reportedly already eroded sharply from a dominant position in early 2026
Extensive and costly ongoing litigation (cash sweep, IPO disclosure, event-contract gambling claims, privacy claims) creates legal-cost and reputational overhang even where settlements are reached
